title: Retirement tests leave no running MySQL server behind

intentCoverage.report:
## Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-114#disposable-mysql-stops-before-cleanup

**Outcome: Assertion gap.** With the fault in place, both helper test files still passed (9 of 9). An independent observer showed that the fault caused the wrong behavior on the path those tests use: 5 of the 6 disposable servers were still running after their `doughnut-retire-mysql-*` folder had already been removed. The baseline and restored runs showed this for 0 of 6.

### What was checked
- **Story and revision:** `.planning/seeds/SEED-114-disposable-mysql-cleanup.md#disposable-mysql-stops-before-cleanup`, key example "Cleanup waits for the server": the cleanup returns only after that `mysqld` has exited and its folder is gone. Checked at revision `37253a42ccbf19ab0026b67c1168da2933f6e9fe`, in a scratch worktree at `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/3fbbabd2/tmp/intent-scratch`, created from that revision and removed afterwards.
- **Fault (one edit):** in `scripts/worktree-retirement-disposable-mysql.mjs`, inside `stop`, line 160 changed from `await terminateOwnedProcessTree({` to `terminateOwnedProcessTree({`. This is a dropped `await`. Because `terminateOwnedProcessTree` awaits `captureDescendants()` first, the `rmSync(home, …)` call now runs before `SIGTERM` is even sent, and `stop` returns while the server is still running.
- **Fixture and existing protection (both unchanged):** `scripts/worktree-retirement-mutation.test.mjs` (6 tests) and `scripts/worktree-retirement-e2e-mutation.test.mjs` (3 tests). Each test that starts a server calls `startDisposableMysql(t)`, which registers `stop` with `t.after`. These tests have no assertion about whether the server has exited. Their only protection is that `node:test` fails a test when its after-hook throws. With the old code, that happened when `rmSync` raised `ENOTEMPTY`, as in the story's evidence.
- **Focused command (identical in all three runs, run from the scratch checkout):** `CURSOR_DEV=true nix --extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes' develop -c node --test scripts/worktree-retirement-mutation.test.mjs scripts/worktree-retirement-e2e-mutation.test.mjs`
- **Independent observer:** a separate Node poller outside the checkout. Every 30 ms it ran `ps -axww`, found helper `mysqld` processes by their `--datadir=…/doughnut-retire-mysql-*/data` argument, recorded each process's parent command, and checked whether the folder still existed. Each server's parent command was the `node --test` child for one of the two test files, so all observed servers belonged to these runs.

### Run observations (macOS host shared with other sessions, very high load)
| Run | 1-min load | Tests | `ENOTEMPTY` | Servers seen | Seen running after folder removed | Longest time running after removal | `pgrep -fl doughnut-retire-mysql-` afterwards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | 36.47 | 9 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped | none | 6 | 0 | n/a | empty |
| Fault | 36.96 | 9 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped | none | 6 | 5 (pids 44948, 45064, 52896, 62446, 63248) | 557 ms (pid 63248); 548 ms and 503 ms for two others | empty |
| Restored | 41.27 | 9 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped | none | 6 | 0 | n/a | empty |

- **Reach:** the faulted `stop` ran through the tests' `t.after` hooks. Every server's folder was removed during the run, and only `stop` removes it. In the fault run, servers started by both test files, for example pid 45064 (mutation) and pid 44948 (e2e-mutation), were seen running with the folder already gone. The maintained check (an after-hook error failing the test) was reached and stayed green.
- **Wrong behavior:** in the fault run, the cleanup returned while its `mysqld` was still running, which breaks the promise. The servers exited later only because the unawaited termination kept running in the background. No server was left at the end, and the temporary folders of all three Nix shells were empty.
- **Limit:** with this fault, `rmSync` runs on an idle running server, before `SIGTERM`. The original bug sent `SIGTERM` first and then raced the shutdown writes. So whether the test files can catch either version depends on an `ENOTEMPTY` race; it did not happen in this run even at load 37. The story's earlier `ENOTEMPTY` failures happened under the 18-file group, not under this 2-file command. This is one fault run, not a frequency measurement.
- **Restoration:** a trap restored the helper with `git checkout -- scripts/worktree-retirement-disposable-mysql.mjs` in the scratch checkout. Afterwards its SHA-256 matched the pre-probe value (`353530956fcab732…`), HEAD was still `37253a42cc`, and `git status --porcelain --ignored` matched the pre-probe state except for the ignored `.claude/skills/` symlinks, which the Nix shell hook created during the baseline run. The restored run passed 9 of 9 (above). The scratch worktree was then removed with `git worktree remove`. The execution checkout stayed clean at `37253a42cc`, with no commits, stashes, or edits there.

### Cost
- **Test runtime.** Measured, from the `node:test` `duration_ms` value: baseline 23,272 ms, fault 20,461 ms, restored 19,116 ms. Measured wall time for each command including `nix develop`, timed with `date` in whole seconds: 42 s, 38 s and 31 s.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable. No human input was requested or measured during this check, and there is no separate measure of human time.
- **Agent effort.** Measured as 19 tool calls by this agent, counted from its own tool use and including this finisher. Token and compute usage are unavailable because they are not visible to the agent.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 318263 ms (measured), from 1794203015185 to 1794203333448 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
